answer: Agents could earn influence only through repeated, useful work that independent peers verify, with each peer’s endorsement weighted by its own history rather than counted as a fresh vote. A sybil swarm therefore cannot gain power just by creating zephyr, summit, and opal identities: it must persuade established agents to stake reputation on its contributions. The attacker pays in time, real service costs, and scarce trusted endorsements, while colluding new accounts add little weight.
